jurisdiction.name: Czechia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Czechia's AI policy rests on the National AI Strategy 2030, approved by the government in July 2024 and replacing the 2019 strategy, with the EU AI Act applying directly; the national implementing law, which would make the Czech Telecommunication Office the main market surveillance authority, is still a draft. National law regulates real-time remote biometric identification at airports (2025) and creates deepfake offences (in force 2026). The Office of the Government issued a 2026 guide on ethical AI use in public administration, the Justice Ministry has an AI use policy, and the data protection and cyber security authorities have issued AI decisions and guidance, including on the government's 2025 DeepSeek ban.
lead_institutions: National Cyber and Information Security Agency
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The draft AI Act law has not reached parliament and is listed as a lead, and the telecommunications office's website blocked access.

instruments.official_title: Národní strategie umělé inteligence České republiky 2030
instruments.english_title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of the Czech Republic 2030 (NAIS 2030)
instruments.issuing_authority: Government of the Czech Republic (approved by resolution No. 520 of 24 July 2024); prepared by the Ministry of Industry and Trade
instruments.current_status: In force as the national AI strategy. Approved by government resolution No. 520 of 24 July 2024 (stated on the Ministry of Industry and Trade AI page, which also hosts the PDF and, since 2026, annexes 2 and 3 on labour-market impacts and AI R&D). It supersedes the 2019 strategy. Annual action plans are approved within the Digital Czechia implementation plans (the 2025 plan by resolution No. 237 of 2 April 2025; the plan documents themselves were not found online, see leads).
instruments.summary: Update of the 2019 national AI strategy, setting the vision and goals to 2030 in seven interlinked areas: AI in research, development and innovation; education and expertise; skills and labour-market impacts; ethical and legal aspects (including supervisory capacity for EU AI Act enforcement and soft-law tools); security aspects; AI in industry and business; and AI in public administration and public services. It defines the institutional framework, with the Ministry of Industry and Trade as coordinator and the AI Committee (Výbor pro umělou inteligenci, a working group of the Committee for the Digital Economy and Society) overseeing implementation through annual action plans within the Digital Czechia implementation plans.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy; anchors annual NAIS action plans and Czech AI Act implementation work.

The approval by government resolution No. 314 of 6 May 2019 is stated in NAIS 2030; the Ministry of Industry and Trade page says the strategy was approved in May 2019.
instruments.summary: The Czech Republic's first national AI strategy, with the vision of making Czechia a 'model country for Europe' in AI, built on industry, defence and security. Its seven chapters covered research and development, investment and financing of the AI ecosystem, AI in industry and services, education and human capital, labour-market impacts, and legal and societal aspects including ethics and consumer protection. It led to the creation of the AI Committee to coordinate implementation.

instruments.english_title: Act No. 230/2025 Coll. amending Act No. 273/2008 Coll. on the Police of the Czech Republic and certain other acts (incl. new §§ 39a-39c of the Personal Data Processing Act on 'isolated' real-time remote biometric identification AI systems at international airports)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of the Interior (Collection of Laws, e-Sbírka)
instruments.current_status: In force from 1 August 2025 (most provisions; a few unrelated points from 1 July 2027). Promulgated in the Collection of Laws on 10 July 2025. The Office for Personal Data Protection reports that, following this amendment, the Police facial-recognition system at Prague airport was deactivated on 1 August 2025 and its biometric data deleted.
instruments.summary: Omnibus police law of 11 June 2025 whose Article IX amends Act No. 110/2019 Coll. by inserting §§ 39a-39c on an 'isolated system', defined as an AI system for real-time remote biometric identification under Art. 3(42) of the EU AI Act, used by a law-enforcement authority only within the premises of an international airport. Use is limited to the AI Act Art. 5 objectives (searching for victims and missing persons, suspects of Annex II offences punishable by at least 4 years, preventing imminent threats to life and terrorist attacks), requires prior written authorisation by a High Court judge for up to 12 months (with a fundamental-rights impact assessment summary and EU database registration), a 24-hour notification to a supervising officer for each person entered in the reference database, deletion after 90 days and a report to the Office for Personal Data Protection within 72 hours of first use.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First Czech statute with explicit AI Act-based rules; national legal basis for law-enforcement real-time biometric identification (AI Act Art. 5(5)).

instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of the Interior (Collection of Laws, e-Sbírka)
instruments.current_status: In force since its promulgation on 24 April 2019; amended several times, including by Act No. 230/2025 Coll. (AI biometric identification at airports, from 1 August 2025).
instruments.summary: National data protection law of 12 March 2019 that implements the GDPR, transposes the Law Enforcement Directive (EU) 2016/680 and establishes the Office for Personal Data Protection. § 39 permits a competent law-enforcement authority to take action affecting a data subject's rights based solely on automated processing only where another law expressly provides for it; it also governs data protection impact assessments and prior consultation (§§ 37-38). Since 1 August 2025 (Act No. 230/2025 Coll.) §§ 39a-39c regulate real-time remote biometric identification AI systems at international airports.

instruments.official_title: Policie ČR (UOOU-04892/21) - Kamerový systém na letišti Václava Havla Praha
instruments.english_title: Police of the Czech Republic (UOOU-04892/21): camera system at Václav Havel Airport Prague - inspection findings on automated facial recognition
instruments.current_status: Inspection concluded in 2025 (file UOOU-04892/21); the Office's published summary gives only the year. The Police informed the Office that the system was deactivated on 1 August 2025 and all biometric data deleted, following the amendment of Act No. 110/2019 Coll. by Act No. 230/2025 Coll.
instruments.summary: Inspection, concluded in 2025, of the Police's automated biometric facial-recognition system at Prague airport, which compared faces captured by cameras with a reference database of 'persons of interest'. The Office found the processing breached Art. 10 of the Law Enforcement Directive because the Police Act gives no explicit legal basis for processing biometric data for unique identification, and that biometric indexes of all persons were kept longer than necessary (this second finding was later set aside on the Police's objections); the President of the Office confirmed the other findings.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First Czech regulator finding on police use of AI facial recognition; led to the system's deactivation when the 2025 statutory regime took effect.

instruments.official_title: ÚOOÚ k biometrické identifikaci nežádoucích osob na fotbalových stadionech
instruments.english_title: Office for Personal Data Protection statement on biometric identification of unwanted persons at football stadiums
instruments.current_status: Published on uoou.gov.cz on 20 May 2026 as a guidance statement; not a binding decision.
instruments.summary: Statement from the Office's consultation practice on camera systems that process biometric data (facial characteristics) to keep banned persons out of football stadiums. It distinguishes ordinary CCTV (legitimate interest under GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)) from biometric identification, which is special-category processing prohibited by Art. 9(1) GDPR unless an Art. 9(2) exception applies, and sets out the strict conditions and risks (permanence of biometric data, misuse) that operators must assess before deploying such systems.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Regulator guidance on biometric (facial recognition) systems in private venues.

instruments.english_title: Methodological material on government resolution No. 537 of 9 July 2025 banning DeepSeek products, applications and services
instruments.issuing_authority: National Cyber and Information Security Agency (NÚKIB)
instruments.publisher_name: National Cyber and Information Security Agency
instruments.current_status: Version 1.0 dated 9 July 2025 (listed on nukib.gov.cz on 14 July 2025). The underlying government resolution No. 537 of 9 July 2025 is binding on state administration bodies; its own text was not found on an official site (see leads).
instruments.summary: NÚKIB guidance implementing government resolution No. 537 of 9 July 2025, which requires ministries, offices and other state administration bodies not to use products, applications, solutions, websites and web services (including the API) of the Chinese AI company DeepSeek in exercising their powers or on state-owned devices. It explains the security grounds (weak security, storage of user data in China and Russia, subjection to Chinese law enabling state access, links of the parent company to the Communist Party of China), defines the bodies covered and gives practical steps for blocking and removal, with a published list of DeepSeek network indicators.

instruments.english_title: New AI frontier models significantly increase the ability to autonomously detect and exploit vulnerabilities: misuse by malicious actors is a matter of time (situation report)
instruments.issuing_authority: National Cyber and Information Security Agency (NÚKIB)
instruments.publisher_name: National Cyber and Information Security Agency
instruments.current_status: Dated Brno, 18 June 2026; listed in NÚKIB analyses on 29 June 2026. Analytical guidance, not binding.
instruments.summary: NÚKIB situation report assessing cybersecurity-focused frontier AI models (citing Anthropic's Mythos, April 2026) that can find, validate and chain software vulnerabilities at scale. It judges it almost certain that such capabilities will reach state and non-state attackers and very likely that they will shorten the time between discovery and exploitation, raising incident numbers in Czechia. It recommends effective vulnerability reporting and handling, rapid prioritisation of the riskiest weaknesses and, later, use of such tools to test one's own infrastructure.

instruments.english_title: Ethical and Responsible Use of AI in Public Administration - Guide for authorities and other public administration organisations
instruments.issuing_authority: Section for the State Service, Office of the Government of the Czech Republic (guarantor), with an author team from the Czech Metrology Institute, Czech Telecommunication Office, Digital and Information Agency, Ministry of Industry and Trade, Ministry of the Interior, NÚKIB and others
instruments.publisher_name: Office of the Government of the Czech Republic
instruments.current_status: 1st edition, February 2026 (only the month is stated in the document). Non-binding guidance; described as a 'living' document to be updated.
instruments.summary: First edition (February 2026, legal status as of February 2026) of a 45-page guide for civil servants, managers and methodologists on using AI in public administration. Part I sets AI basics and a 'minimum standard' for ethical and responsible AI use built on principles linked to the 2023 Code of Ethics of State Employees (AI as a tool, not a replacement for staff); Part II covers the legal framework (EU AI Act, GDPR) and safe work, quality assurance and checking of outputs; Part III covers AI governance, roles and responsibilities in public bodies, including internal rules for introducing and operating AI. It states that it is not a binding regulation but a support for organisations of all sizes.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Central-government guidance on public-sector AI use, ethics and governance.

instruments.english_title: Ministry of Justice Instruction No. 11/2025 of 9 December 2025 amending Instruction No. 5/2022 on information security in the ICT environment of the justice sector (adds Policy No. 25 on the use of artificial intelligence)
instruments.current_status: In force from 15 December 2025 (Article II); signed by the Minister of Justice.
instruments.summary: Internal instruction that adds Policy No. 25 'Use of Artificial Intelligence' to the justice sector's information-security rules, binding on all staff of the justice sector (and to be reflected in contracts with partners). It defines AI platforms and tools, allows only AI tools approved by the cyber security manager (currently only Microsoft Copilot on the ministry's secured tenant, with data kept in the EU and not used for training), sets data-minimisation rules for prompts, permits only certain data classification levels to be entered (entering 'especially sensitive' data is prohibited), and bans unapproved AI tools except by reasoned written exception.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding sector-wide AI use policy for the justice sector (ministry and justice bodies).

instruments.official_title: Zákon č. 270/2025 Sb., kterým se mění zákon č. 40/2009 Sb., trestní zákoník, ve znění pozdějších předpisů, zákon č. 141/1961 Sb., o trestním řízení soudním (trestní řád), ve znění pozdějších předpisů, a další související zákony
instruments.english_title: Act No. 270/2025 Coll. amending the Criminal Code, the Criminal Procedure Code and related acts (new deepfake offences: § 181(2) and § 191a of the Criminal Code)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of the Interior (Collection of Laws, e-Sbírka)
instruments.current_status: Promulgated 5 August 2025; the Criminal Code provisions (Art. I, incl. points 60-63 and 73) take effect on 1 January 2026. The provisions are technology-neutral (the text does not mention AI) but target realistic fabricated depictions of real persons.
instruments.summary: Criminal-law amendment of 3 July 2025 that, among many changes, creates two offences targeting deepfakes. New § 181(2) punishes (up to two years, more if spread via a public computer network) whoever, intending to cause serious harm to another's rights, produces or disseminates a work that without authorisation depicts or uses another person's likeness or personal expression and appears genuine although the perpetrator knows it is not. New § 191a ('misuse of identity to produce pornography and its dissemination') punishes producing or distributing pornographic works depicting or using a person who did not consent, with higher penalties for online dissemination.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Criminal offences for harmful synthetic media (deepfakes), including AI-generated pornography.

changes.title: Rules on airport real-time remote biometric identification AI systems take effect
changes.detail: Act No. 230/2025 Coll. takes effect on 1 August 2025 (first day of the month after promulgation).

changes.title: Act No. 230/2025 Coll. (airport real-time biometric identification AI systems) promulgated
changes.detail: Promulgated in the Collection of Laws on 10 July 2025; inserts §§ 39a-39c into Act No. 110/2019 Coll.

changes.title: Government bans DeepSeek in state administration; NÚKIB issues implementing guidance
changes.detail: Government resolution No. 537 of 9 July 2025; NÚKIB methodological material v1.0 dated 9 July 2025.

changes.title: Government approves National AI Strategy of the Czech Republic 2030
changes.detail: Approved by government resolution No. 520 of 24 July 2024; supersedes the 2019 strategy.

changes.title: 2019 National AI Strategy superseded by NAIS 2030
changes.detail: Replaced by the National AI Strategy of the Czech Republic 2030 (resolution No. 520 of 24 July 2024).

leads.title: Návrh zákona o umělé inteligenci
leads.english_title: Draft Act on Artificial Intelligence (national implementing law for the EU AI Act)
leads.note: Government bill prepared by the Ministry of Industry and Trade (gestor of the EU AI Act since 28 May 2025) to designate national supervisory authorities (the Czech Telecommunication Office as main market-surveillance authority, with the Czech National Bank, the Office for Personal Data Protection and the Office for Technical Standardization, Metrology and State Testing) and set sanctions and a sandbox. Inter-ministerial comment procedure reported from late September 2025. Not found among the Chamber of Deputies prints of the 10th term (searched all 687 print entries on psp.cz on 2026-10-12), so it had not reached Parliament; draft text not located on an official open portal. Record when introduced or adopted.

leads.title: Usnesení vlády č. 537 ze dne 9. července 2025 o zákazu produktů, aplikací a služeb DeepSeek
leads.english_title: Government resolution No. 537 of 9 July 2025 banning DeepSeek products, applications and services in state administration
leads.note: Binding on ministries, offices and other state administration bodies; described in the NÚKIB methodological material (recorded). Resolution text not located on the government resolutions database during this review; record as administrative_policy_mandatory_in_scope once read.

leads.title: Akční plán Národní strategie umělé inteligence ČR 2030 (pro rok 2025; Akční plán 2027 v přípravě)
leads.english_title: Action Plan of the National AI Strategy 2030 (2025 plan; 2027 plan in preparation)
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Industry and Trade / Government of the Czech Republic
leads.note: The 2025 action plan was approved as part of the Digital Czechia implementation plan by government resolution No. 237 of 2 April 2025 (MPO news page, 2 April 2025), allocating CZK 19 billion to project plans. The action plan document itself is not attached on mpo.gov.cz; record once the official text is found.

leads.title: Usnesení vlády č. 394 ze dne 28. května 2025 k zajištění národní implementace nařízení o umělé inteligenci
leads.english_title: Government resolution No. 394 of 28 May 2025 on national implementation of the EU AI Act (MPO as AI Act lead; ČTÚ among market-surveillance authorities)
leads.note: Cited in the Czech Telecommunication Office's 2025 annual report (resolution No. 394 of 28 May 2025 designating ČTÚ as one of the AI Act market-surveillance authorities) and on the MPO AI page (MPO designated AI Act gestor on 28 May 2025; ÚOOÚ and the Public Defender of Rights as Art. 77 bodies). Resolution text not read; record as government-governance once found.

leads.title: Český telekomunikační úřad - sekce Umělá inteligence (informace k Aktu o umělé inteligenci, čl. 50, srpen 2026)
leads.english_title: Czech Telecommunication Office AI section and notices on the EU AI Act (incl. Art. 50 transparency obligations, August 2026)
leads.note: ČTÚ's 2025 annual report says it created a dedicated AI section on its website, an expert team and held an AI Act workshop; press reports an August 2026 ČTÚ notice on Art. 50 transparency duties and an internal measure (Opatření č. 37/2025) on staff AI use. ctu.gov.cz returned HTTP 403 to all automated requests on 2026-10-12 (the annual report was read via WebFetch only), so these pages could not be read.

leads.title: Doporučení pro využívání umělé inteligence na základních a středních školách
leads.english_title: Recommendations for the use of AI in primary and secondary schools (with versions for principals and pupils; 2025 FAQ 'AI a právo ve škole')
leads.issuing_authority: National Pedagogical Institute of the Czech Republic (NPI ČR, MŠMT)
leads.note: Published on the NPI digitalizace.rvp.cz portal (https://digitalizace.rvp.cz/ke-stazeni#doporuceni-pro-ai; PDF https://revize.edu.cz/files/ai-doporuceni-online-a4.pdf, read). Sets recommendations in seven areas (open communication, individualisation, AI literacy, responsibility for outputs, children's rights and privacy, proportionality, wellbeing). The document and page state no publication date (PDF metadata 2023-08-29), and the MŠMT news page about NPI's AI materials returned 'page not found'; record as nonbinding_guidance (education) once an official dated listing is found.

leads.title: Memorandum o spolupráci při zavádění AI do zdravotnictví / resortní strategie AI ve zdravotnictví
leads.english_title: Ministry of Health memorandum on safe use of AI in healthcare (2026) and planned health-sector AI strategy
leads.note: Ministry of Health press releases (mzd.gov.cz) report a 2026 cooperation memorandum with the Czech Association for AI, the Czech Medical Association J. E. Purkyně and IPVZ on rules for safe AI use in healthcare, and a national survey (February 2026) feeding a planned sector AI strategy. No memorandum or strategy text found; record when published.

leads.title: ČSN EN ISO/IEC 42001 Informační technologie - Umělá inteligence - Systém managementu
leads.english_title: Czech adoption of EN ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management system standard)
leads.issuing_authority: Czech Standards Agency (Česká agentura pro standardizaci)
leads.note: Commercial catalogues list the Czech edition as issued 1 September 2026; not confirmed on the Czech Standards Agency catalogue or the ÚNMZ bulletin during this review. Record under standards once the official listing is read.
